note: The known deviations: the places where the system and the field, or the
system and itself, do not agree, and what each one is worth.
A deviation is a fact about the system, not a task. The field's own
implementations differ from the system's elements, and that is a
difference the contract records rather than a hole to close. A debt the
field owes is a debt the field owns: it is named here with its
severity so that a reader knows what weighs on the system, and the
numbers live in the audit, which is regenerated by measurement.
critical  the contract is wrong, or a consumer would render something
major     the contract is incomplete, and a consumer would have to guess
minor     the field and the contract differ in a way that is deliberate
none      a difference that is not a deviation
A closed deviation carries a probe: the command's finding that the
difference has not come back. The gate runs the probe, so a closed
deviation cannot reopen without the gate saying so.

deviations.what: The published sheet declared thirteen of its custom properties as references to themselves, which is invalid at computed-value time.
One of the sheet's roles still carried a colour of its own instead of naming the system's step.
The field's three spellings — the action, the state and the section — are the field's own implementations, and they differ from the system's button, badge and section-heading.
The package carried the field's vocabulary and not the system's own elements, so a consumer that had adopted it could not use the contract's elements at all.
The audit stated that the path blob.in-showcase's audit cites does not exist. It does exist: the file is there, and what it carries is a palette that is not the system's.

gnu.in.work carries the largest debt in the field: 1966 colours the contract does not have and a thousand and nine components of its own, of which the directory ee/ holds 526 under the FSL-1.1 licence. That directory is out of the programme of the absorption: its Competing Use clause makes it a question of consent, not of technique.

diagram.studio carries 140 colours the contract does not have — the gate now measures the source git follows, and the Mermaid bundle and the unpacked AppImage are not the consumer's interface — and 73 components of its own, of which seventeen are the system's elements under another spelling. Its code is a fork of GitDiagram (MIT, 2024, Ahmed Khaleel) and it redistributes shadcn, Radix, lucide, Mermaid and four OFL fonts without a single notice.

The GPUI launcher carries 299 colours the contract does not have, and thirty-four components of its own. Its licence is not yet a fact: the root says AGPL-3.0 and forty-seven crate manifests say GPL-3.0-or-later. The repository's name is a former one and is not used here; the git remote carries it.
The two reference repositories are archived and read-only, so nothing can be absorbed into them and they will not take the contract's components.
spjoaillerie-live is a capture of a storefront with a brand of its own, and it is not a consumer of this system.
The system had no radius scale: its own components carried six different radii written as numbers, and the field rounds every surface on its own.

The In-Shell's scale of spacing has three steps the system's does not — twenty, forty and eighty. The decision was already taken: the ten steps stand, and a frontend's own scale is mapped onto them. The three are mapped, not inserted, because an ordered scale that is published does not renumber itself in the middle.

The native profile carried tokens and roles and no states, while the contract's own elements declare ten of them. The profile's doctrine says that roles and state cross the boundary and the structure does not, and the states were the half that was missing. The profile now names every state the contract declares, says what each one means, the role it wears and the evidence a native target must produce.

The contract states the envelope's invariants — SUR-002 to SUR-010 — but nothing proves them. The system's own prototype of the envelope applies fifteen of the eighteen statements as failures and holds six by inspection alone: the curvature's global authority, the trigger's internality, the policies' independence per output, the topology's neutrality, the epoch's isolation and the workarea's explicitness. A surface that breaks those six would look right and pass.
The README counted sixteen obligations while the contract carried twenty-three: the count was prose, and prose drifts. It now reads what the contract holds, and a probe holds it there.

The semantic state colours failed on the light substrate, and nothing in the system was looking. On the light surface (#E9E9E6) the attention amber measured 1.68:1, the breach red 3.22:1 and the stable green 2.12:1 — a normal-sized text needs 4.5:1. The contract's contrast table held seven pairings and every one of them was a brand colour, so the semantic colours and the surface ramps were not in it, and the eye rendered no state element to look at. The field's axe run found it: the portal's live route failed colour-contrast on g6-state--attention. Closed by giving the semantic family a step for the light substrate, pointing the light theme's states at it, putting the states into the contrast table, and adding a rule and a probe that hold them there.

The information colour was a single tint for both substrates, and it measured 2.94:1 against the light surface — below the 3:1 a graphic needs, so an information mark would not have been seen on the light substrate's raised surface. It now wears a deeper tint there, which measures 4.36:1.

A consumer could declare a scheme whose values it does not know — a wallpaper decides them — and the contract had no way to read the promise. It audited the fixed values and said nothing about the part that runs, so a derived ink could be declared, never measured, and still count as absorbed.
deviations.proof: core/DERIVATIONS.json states the computations the contract admits, each with the floor it guarantees; tools/audit_scheme.py reads a derived role at its floor against every pairing minimum, and a clamped derivation is admitted only with the deviation that carries its proof. The probe recomputes the floor from the system's own inks.

deviations.what: The launcher's accent comes from the wallpaper, and the ink written on it is chosen against that accent. The system's own two inks guarantee 4.087:1 against a ground the system cannot see — enough for a mark and short of the 4.5 a text role is read at — so the launcher clamps the derived accent's tone until the better of the two inks reaches 4.5. The clamp runs in the launcher, on a colour the contract never sees: the contract can read the declaration and the fallback, not the computation on a given wallpaper.
deviations.proof: engine/gnosis-gpui-theme/src/palette.rs — the clamp, and the test that walks the accent's tone range and measures the better of the two inks on every stop
